newsitem.title: UK: BASKETBALL-EUROPEAN CHAMPIONS PANATHINAIKOS IN SETBACK.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-EUROPEAN CHAMPIONS PANATHINAIKOS IN SETBACK.

text.p: EuroLeague basketball champions Panathinaikos met a surprise setback on Thursday, losing 88-81 away to underdogs Dynamo Moscow.

In the second stage of the competition which pairs the first-phase high-flyers in round-robin action with the early season strugglers from another group, the Greek club were expected to beat a side with a 2-8 record from their 10 games before Thursday's match.
But Dynamo led 46-43 at halftime and held on well to give themselves some renewed hope of reaching the round of the last 16.

In Athens, Olympiakos restored Greek pride, dismantling CSKA Moscow 82-51 with a dazzling second half performance which yielded 47 points to just 18 from the Russian club. Christian Welp top-scored with 19 points.
After a disappointing first phase before Christmas which saw Olympiakos finish fifth in their group, their fervent Greek fans can look to better things.

Turkey's Efes Pilsen now boast the best record in the EuroLeague after stretching their record to 9-2 from 11 matches with a narrow 73-72 win at whipping-boys Bayer Leverkusen (0-11) in group H on Wednesday.
Remarkably, the other two matches in the group, played on Thursday, were also decided by a single point.
Last year's runners-up Barcelona edged by Kinder Bologna, also 73-72, while in a game played in Pesaro, Italy, for security reasons Split of Croatia beat Partizan Belgrade 76-75.
